A closes its text area at a 1px #DFDFDF rule at y=1748 with ~34px clear, so a line is never guillotined mid-glyph at the window edge (and A gives you '188 words' at the bottom; B gives you nothing).
gapTheirs: Markers sit inside the text column, so the page has three different left edges: body starts at x=622, H1 'The Lighthouse' at x=673 (+51px), H2 'What the sea keeps' at x=697 (+75px). B hangs '#' at 570, '##' at 546 and '-' at 576 out in the margin so every line — heading, body, list — starts flush at x=623, one edge.
verdict: Same paper, same ink, same measure, same caret — so the whole thing turns on the left edge, and A loses it. A's hash marks live inside the column, so the H1 kicks 51px right of the paragraph beneath it and the H2 kicks 75px right: three left edges on a page whose only job is holding one, and you re-notice it every time you scroll past a heading. B hangs the markers in the margin and everything lines up at x=623, which is the difference between a manuscript and a text field, and it buys back the ~116px (6.4% of the viewport) A spends on a title bar and a hairline-ruled word-count strip — two more lines of your own prose. B's frame is still lopsided, 168px of air on top and zero at the bottom, which is sloppy, but a sheared last line is a scroll artefact; a ragged left edge is the design.

states.gap: No top edge to the page: the H1 ink starts at y=168 of 1800 (9.3% of the viewport) against B's y=238 (13.2%), and A's own paragraph gap is 148px — so the title floats only 20px more than an ordinary blank line and reads as mid-document, not as the top of a page; the bottom is worse, with 0px gutter, the last list line sliced through its x-height at row 1799.
states.gapTheirs: ~145px of the 1800px page (8%) is spent on app furniture in a second, proportional typeface: a 60px 'Untitled.md' title bar and an 85px footer reading '188 words 961 characters 1 min read'. It costs B a full text line and the entire bullet list, which A reaches at y=1722 in the identical viewport — a live scoreboard on a page that should only be holding sentences.
states.verdict: B's left margin zigzags: body text sets at x=142, but '#' and '##' sit inline so the heading words start at 193 and 211 — a 51px and 69px stagger at every heading, while A hangs its markers out at 128 and 104 and keeps one unbroken 181px edge from the title through the body to the '-' of the list. B is also the looser measure at 1621px / 62 characters against A's 1539px / 58, which is the wrong direction to loosen when you're already at the top of the comfortable band. A is a page; B is a page inside an app that keeps telling you your word count while you're trying to find the next sentence.
